::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Oct 8 1866  
**Manuscript:** Copy outletter book British Library Add MSS.55386 (1) P. 451
:::

My dear Miss Yonge                                                              Oct 8 1866

I have a good many things to write to you about, but I am going to confine myself at present to one.

You remember our projected [Sunday Library](organizations/other_145.qmd) and the several difficulties we found among those writers quite adequate for various subjects, a free Church Minister in Glasgow has written a series of papers on Natural History subjects (he is an accomplished naturalist) connected with the Bible. He has sent me one and I have agreed to publish. There is a collected form under the title of Bible Readings in Nature or in the Knowledge of Nature.[^1] I have read through a good many of them aloud to my wife &amp; children. They strike me as realizing so completely the idea I had in seeking to make a Sunday Library that I cannot help sending them to you at once for your opinion of them. I won’t say another word about them, or any thing else at present. But I shall be glad to hear what you think of them on the whole.

Yours very faithfully

A. Macmillan

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

---

[^1]: This is probably a reference to the Rev. Hugh Macmillan, *Bible Teachings in Nature* (1867).  In 1861 Macmillan had published another book by the same author (to whom he was related) entitled *Footnotes from the Page of Nature*.
